title: Self Driving Products: Product Signals to Pull Requests — Joshua Snyder, PostHog
talk_summary: PostHog describes a pipeline that turns product observability signals (errors, session replays, Slack) into grouped 'reports', runs a research agent to diagnose them, then an execution agent in a sandbox that pushes a PR and iterates until CI is green. Key lessons: normalize signals before embedding, gate on actionability so agents don't fix vague problems, and don't over-optimize token cost before you've seen agent behavior.

takeaways.technique: Actionability gate before dispatching an agent
takeaways.what_they_do: After research, a classification step decides: not actionable (return to pool for more evidence), needs human input (inbox), or immediately actionable (agent writes fix). Vague problems are dropped rather than handed to a coder.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you just throw an agent at a problem, it will try to fix something ... if not, I should ignore it

takeaways.technique: Embed LLM-generated queries, not raw heterogeneous signals
takeaways.what_they_do: Off-the-shelf embeddings cluster by structural similarity (all stack traces together, all Slack messages together), so they generate a few natural-language queries per signal with an LLM and match those in embedding space instead.

takeaways.technique: Snapshot-and-rehydrate sandbox to iterate PR to green
takeaways.what_they_do: Execution agent clones repo in a sandbox, pushes PR; on CI failure or a review comment it snapshots the sandbox and rehydrates it to continue the same session until the PR is green.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we snapshot the sandbox ... we will rehydrate that snapshot and continue running until the PR is green

takeaways.technique: Explore expensively, then collapse agent steps into one-shot calls
takeaways.what_they_do: They initially avoided agents to save tokens, which was a mistake; running the same problem many times reveals repeatable patterns that can be replaced by a single LLM call or a small trained model.

takeaways.technique: Eval on representative production data, not local vibe checks
takeaways.what_they_do: They stopped testing the pipeline on their own data with a vibe check and moved to representative customer data, because a pipeline ingesting varied real inputs can't be tuned by eyeballing.

takeaways.technique: LLM classifier at pipeline ingress for untrusted signals
takeaways.what_they_do: Because some signal sources are public (e.g. website errors an attacker can trigger), an LLM classifier at the top of the pipeline drops signals attempting prompt injection or abuse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at the moment right at the top of the pipeline is an LLM classifier that's going to check is this trying to do something bad?
